library_preparation_preflight.summary: json-smart 2.4.5 depends on net.minidev:accessors-smart:2.4.3. That version has a POM on Maven Central but no JAR (the JAR URL returns 404), so testCompileClasspath cannot resolve. Adding accessors-smart 2.4.6 as a test dependency wins Gradle's highest-version conflict resolution and resolves to a published JAR.

deterministic_setup.reason: accessors-smart:2.4.3, which json-smart 2.4.5 pulls in transitively, was published without a JAR. Declaring 2.4.6 directly makes Gradle resolve that version in its place.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: No environment variables, system properties or Docker images are needed. Keep the existing 2.4.4 tests unchanged. Check that the test build resolves accessors-smart to 2.4.6, not 2.4.3. If the transitive 2.4.3 still wins, force the version with a resolutionStrategy or constraint in the test build.gradle, or exclude accessors-smart from json-smart and declare 2.4.6 explicitly. accessors-smart 2.4.6 uses asm 9.1, and accessors-smart 2.4.6 is the version json-smart 2.4.6 uses.
risks: accessors-smart 2.4.6 differs slightly from the 2.4.3 that json-smart 2.4.5 declares. The 2.4.5 tests then run against a different accessors-smart than the POM specifies, though it is API-compatible.
If Gradle still selects 2.4.3 because of the dependency mediation setup, the resolution failure will persist until the version is forced.
